papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory à la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

papers.title: Lifting the local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and $n\ge 1$ an integer. We construct a local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$, following an approach by Shiho. More precisely, consider the ring $W$ of Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic $p$. Let $f:\mathfrak{X}\rightarrow \mathfrak{S}$ be a log smooth morphism of fs logarithmic $p$-adic formal schemes, whose underlying formal schemes are flat and locally of finite type over $W$, and assume the exact relative Frobenius after reduction modulo $p$ admits a lift $F$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be Lorenzon's indexed algebra on the reduction modulo $p^n$ of $\mathfrak{X}.$ We define an indexed subalgebra $\mathcal{B}_F\subset\mathcal{A}$ and equip it with an integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connection. Our main result is an equivalence between the category of indexed $\mathcal{B}_F$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connections compatible with the $p$-connection on $\mathcal{B}_F$, and the category of indexed $\mathcal{A}$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent connections compatible with the canonical connection on $\mathcal{A}$. This gives a local logarithmic version of the Cartier transform modulo $p^n$.

papers.title: On König's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
papers.abstract: König conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

papers.title: Phase-conjugate Gaussian encoding for continuous-variable quantum key distribution with a single phase-sensitive amplifier
papers.abstract: Phase-conjugate encoding is naturally compatible with shared phase-sensitive amplification and joint detection, offering a compact optical receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD). Here, we develop a unified encoding and security framework for two-mode Gaussian CVQKD with tunable phase-conjugate intermode correlations matched to a joint receiver comprising a single phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) and one balanced photodetector. We present both coherent-state and squeezed-state prepare-and-measure protocols that use the same transmitted ensemble. The two preparations can be implemented through classically precoded Gaussian displacements of coherent sidebands or a directly generated two-mode squeezed vacuum, respectively, without an actual optical mode converter. The encoding and detection scheme separates low-variance joint quadratures for key generation from high-variance joint quadratures carrying private random modulation. This complementary modulation can reduce Eve's Holevo information without changing the Alice--Bob mutual information. Numerical results show that optimized correlated coherent-state encoding achieves higher asymptotic key rates at long distances and extends the positive-key range compared with optimized single-mode coherent-state modulation. The optimal intermode correlation increases with transmission distance, and the range advantage persists under the symmetric correlated two-mode Gaussian attacks considered here. These results provide a theoretical basis for the design and implementation of PSA-enhanced two-mode CVQKD with phase-conjugate encoding.

papers.title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. The extension has four branch points, with inertia groups of orders $2$, $2$, $3$, $3$, and it is the only extension with these properties up to a rational change of the coordinate $t$. We give an explicit polynomial of degree $65$ for it.

papers.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions for a class of fractional Schrödinger equations in $\mathbb R$
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions $u\in H^s(\mathbb R)$ of the fractional Schrödinger equation $(-Δ)^su+λu=f(u)$ in $\mathbb R$, where $0<s<1$, $λ>0$, and $f$ is a general nonlinearity such that $f(t)/t$ is increasing. We prove that, under a single concavity condition on an auxiliary function, positive solutions are unique up to translations. The result applies to all positive solutions rather than only to ground states, and it allows $f'$ to be unbounded below at zero. It covers pure powers, sums of powers, logarithmic and saturable nonlinearities, for suitable ranges of the parameters. We further prove that every positive solution is nondegenerate, with the kernel of the linearized operator spanned by $u'$, and that it has Morse index one. If moreover $f(\sqrt h)/\sqrt h$ is concave, then for $1/2\le s<1$ a positive solution with prescribed $L^2$ norm is unique together with its Lagrange multiplier. The proofs are purely variational, using neither a continuation argument in $s$ nor the nondegeneracy of the linearized operator. Our method rests on the convexity of the action along an interpolation between symmetric decreasing functions that preserves a suitable integral quantity, and this convexity allows us to identify every positive solution as a constrained minimizer. For $1/2\le s<1$ we use the height interpolation of Delgadino, Yan and Yao, while for $0<s<1/2$ we introduce a new two-level interpolation.

papers.title: Goldman's Ergodicity Conjecture and Branched Developing Maps
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation $ρ:π_1(Σ_g)\rightarrow\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$ which sends every simple closed curve to a hyperbolic element admits a branched developing map. As a corollary, the mapping class group action on the Euler class zero component of the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$-character variety of a genus $g$ surface is ergodic if $g\geq3$. (The action is not ergodic if $g=2$.) Moreover, almost every representation of nonzero Euler class admits a branched developing map.

papers.title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
papers.abstract: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut. The eigenbasis is indexed by an $m$-tuple of partitions and an addable corner, whose content is the eigenvalue. We give an anti-normal factorization and prove that the Lax operator is self-adjoint for the transported Euler pairing. With unit framing weight, the rank-one specialization recovers the Nazarov-Sklyanin factorization. We then show that the Lax operator is conjugate to the companion matrix of a projected q-Miura operator of the deformed $W$-algebra of type $\mathfrak{gl}_m$. This also gives an explicit presentation of the $K$-theory of the Hecke correspondence.

papers.title: Block Generalized Inverses in Skew Corner Pairs
papers.abstract: We view generalized inverses from another perspective, through invertibility in the skew corner bimodules $eRf$ attached to a pair of distinct idempotents $e, f$ of a ring $R$. Many generalized inverses are defined by a system of equations together with conditions on ranges and kernels, which makes them harder to visualize as inverses in the traditional sense. In the language of invertible blocks, however, they become genuine one or two-sided inverses of a suitable compression of the element. We will systematically show how block invertibility in a skew corner $eRf$ can be used to visualize Drazin's $(b,c)$-inverse, which contains the Moore--Penrose, Bott-Duffin $(e,f)$ inverses amongst others. On this foundation we develop a way to produce units of the corner ring from complementary blocks, and transport stable range one across two-sided Peirce decompositions for distinct idempotents.

papers.title: The Optimal Interface Method: A Modelling Paradigm for Two-Body Contact Problems via Optimal Control and $Γ$-convergence
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the derivation of a model governing the equilibrium configuration of two linearly elastic bodies that may come into contact with each other. The contact zone, or coincidence set, is an \emph{a priori} unknown of the model, and the equilibrium configuration is governed by variational inequalities. We introduce a new modelling paradigm in which the contact interface between the two linearly elastic bodies under consideration is now regarded as the \emph{primary variable} of an optimal control problem whose states are the unique solutions of two \emph{independent} unilateral contact problems for which this very contact interface represents the obstacle itself. As a result, the free boundary emerges as the solution of a low-dimensional optimisation problem rather than as the active set of coupled variational inequalities. We establish the existence and uniqueness of optimal controls minimising the reduced cost functional arising from the modelling paradigm introduced beforehand, and we show that the family of marginal energy functionals associated with such model $Γ$-converges to the energy functional associated with the original variational inequalities as the positive \emph{cost parameter} $β$ in the reduced cost functional tends to zero. This $Γ$-convergence argument also yields a characterisation of the coincidence set of the limit problem in terms of the optimal interfaces. We further show that, after a suitable regularisation, the reduced cost functional is Gâteaux differentiable, and that its Gâteaux derivative can be explicitly computed \emph{without solving any adjoint system}. Finally, we corroborate the $Γ$-convergence result obtained beforehand with numerical experiments on a simplified and exactly solvable configuration.

papers.title: Lower bounds for testing the completely depolarizing channel
papers.abstract: We study lower bounds to the query complexity of testing whether an unknown quantum channel mapping a $d_{\mathrm{in}}$-dimensional input to a $d_{\mathrm{out}}$-dimensional output is the completely depolarizing channel or is $\varepsilon$-far from it in diamond distance. We show that for this task (i) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, adaptive tester requires at least $Ω(d_{\mathrm{in}}d_{\mathrm{out}}/\varepsilon^2)$ queries; (ii) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, non-adaptive tester requires at least $\max\{Ω(d_{\mathrm{in}}^{1.5}d_{\mathrm{out}}/\varepsilon^2), Ω(d_{\mathrm{in}}^{2}/\varepsilon^2)\}$ queries. We also show that these lower bounds apply to the more general problem of determining whether an unknown channel belongs to the set of all state-replacement channels or is $\varepsilon$-far from the entire set in diamond distance.

papers.title: On Pairwise Independent and Strongly Correlated Random Variables
papers.abstract: Characterizing joint distributions that maximize the centered third-order moment under prescribed marginal distributions and pairwise independence has various statistical applications. This problem can be formulated as a multistochastic optimal transport problem. In this work, we generalize the results on the $(3,2)$-multistochastic Monge-Kantorovich problem to cost functions of the form $c(x,y,z)=f(x)f(y)f(z)$, where $f$ is defined on $[0,1]$ through dyadic expansions: $f(x)=\sum_{i\geq 1} a_i x_i$, with $x_i\in\{0,1\}$. Under summability and domination conditions on the coefficients, we show that an optimal transport plan is concentrated on the Sierpinski tetrahedron. We also characterize mixtures of geometric coefficient sequences through Hausdorff moment sequences and construct a recursive dual solution with its integral representation for costs with geometric coefficients.

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $Σ_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $Σ_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Relative involutions and inverses in monoidal dualities and slice constructions
papers.abstract: Our goal in this paper is to work towards developing a framework for characterizing dualities of weak categorical structures. It is often the case that duality involutions are characterized by relations which are more general than $f^2=1$. Moreover, it is also true that many dualities cannot be expressed using involutions alone. We develop a framework of relative involutions and relative inverses to express these dualities at least within categorical and bicategorical structures. In particular, we utilize this framework to express the dualities of virtual double categories and some important constructions on them. In the second part, we explore the problem of slicing and consider how dualities of monoidal structures interact with slice constructions. We end by providing a construction for both enriched slice model categories and enriched coslice model categories.

papers.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
papers.abstract: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.

papers.title: Canonical activation patterns and ReLU pattern varieties
papers.abstract: A ReLU pattern variety records the polynomial relations among the coefficients of the affine maps associated with a prescribed set of activation patterns of a ReLU network. We study how the combinatorics of the canonical set of activation patterns of an unbiased ReLU network is reflected in the geometry of its pattern variety. In particular, we introduce the notion of pattern stability and characterize pattern stability and combinatorial stability for shallow networks. When the associated wall graph is connected and contains an edge of every neuron label, we resolve a problem of Alexandr and Montúfar by determining the defining ideal of the associated pattern variety explicitly. We establish a hierarchy of progressively weaker equivalence relations relating labeled combinatorial equivalence, equality and permutation equivalence of canonical pattern sets, and equivalences of the associated varieties. Finally, we relate functional dimension to the differential of the pattern map and show that it is bounded above by the dimension of the canonical pattern variety at every depth. For nondegenerate shallow networks, we give an exact formula for the functional dimension; for every shallow architecture, it equals the dimension of the canonical pattern variety on an open dense set of full Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: The Mézard-Parisi formula for diluted Potts models
papers.abstract: We obtain the Mézard-Parisi formula for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on random uniform hypergraphs, including the Erdős-Rényi graph. The upper bound in the graph case was proved by Contucci, Dommers, Giardinà, and Starr, whose interpolation extends to uniform hypergraphs. Here we prove the matching lower bound for a general class of diluted models with finite spin alphabets. The proof follows closely the corresponding argument for diluted Ising models, so we outline only the adjustments needed for several colors.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.

papers.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+ε})$ gate cost
papers.abstract: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+ε})$. Here $ε>0$ depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a "policy" that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.

papers.title: From decay to regularity: the dispersion generalized Benjamin-Ono equation
papers.abstract: We study the initial value problem associated with the dispersive generalized Benjamin-Ono equation \begin{equation*} \partial_{t}u-\partial_{x}|D_{x}|^{a}u+u\,\partial_{x}u=0,\quad 1<a<2, \end{equation*} in weighted Sobolev spaces. First, we show that if the solution belongs to $L^{2}(|x|^{2α}dx)$ at two different times, then it gains regularity, namely $u\in C([-T,T]:H^{aα}(\mathbb{R}))$, for $α<5/2+a$ and suitable initial regularity. Second, we establish the persistence of the solution flow in $H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{2}(|x|^{2α}dx)$ under the sharp regularity assumption $s\ge aα$, for $α\in[1/2,5/2+a)$, where the zero mean condition is required for $α\ge 3/2+a$. Finally, we prove the unique continuation principles associated with the optimal decay rates $|x|^{3/2+a}$ and $|x|^{5/2+a}$ under optimal regularity assumptions. Our approach relies on weighted energy estimates, commutator expansions for the fractional Laplacian and pseudo-differential calculus.

papers.title: Response-Threshold Framework for First-Peak Preservation in Noisy Grover Search
papers.abstract: Grover search is executed only after integer iterations, so noise can alter the stopping decision even when a continuous first peak remains visible. We develop a response-threshold framework separating continuous peak motion, stroboscopic geometry, and the discrete sampled-success argmax. For a Drude-Lorentz environment, linearized HEOM supplies an a priori timing coefficient and sampled-probability differentials. The first-order layer is used as a conservative screen: well-separated points retain the nominal step, whereas near-threshold points escalate to finite-$λ$ evaluation. Across 260 unique HEOM points drawn from five overlapping validation sets, it detects all 15 observed stopping changes with zero regret on the changed subset; its residual errors are 45 one-step-early calls on otherwise stable points; the 245-point stable subset has mean regret $4.42\times10^{-3}$. An empirically validated two-stage workflow escalates every observed change while avoiding 160 of 260 unique full-HEOM propagations. Same-bath NZ2 reduces early calls. A heterogeneous three-qubit circuit exhibits three stopping-transition scales, each replicated across eight marked targets, and finite-shot recovery is 96.18% overall, with failures localized to a near-degenerate boundary at $s=1.5$. A depth-refined transfer test supports the predicted local quadratic timing-to-loss relation.

papers.title: On Covariance Steering with Nonlinear Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper examines two ways nonlinear measurements complicate the statistical predictions during covariance steering. The covariance steering problem optimizes a control policy across a distribution of possible trajectories rather than a single specific trajectory. This approach has attracted growing interest as a way to account for uncertainty in aerospace applications such as trajectory optimization, stationkeeping, and landing. In many of these applications, covariance steering can account for measurement uncertainty through output feedback. Because standard formulations assume linear dynamics and measurements, applications with nonlinear measurements typically use an extended Kalman filter to estimate the state. This paper shows that techniques used to improve filter convergence, such as measurement underweighting, can reduce the accuracy of conventional covariance steering predictions by violating a key assumption. This is addressed with a new convex formulation that relaxes the assumption. This paper also demonstrates that adjusting the control policy during execution can improve agreement between predicted and actual state statistics. A numerical example of angles-only spacecraft rendezvous illustrates the benefits of the proposed method, and discussions are made regarding the implications of this generalized covariance steering formulation.

papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
papers.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nyström trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

papers.title: 150 years proving fundamental science is worth the wait
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03538-3Founded in 1876, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science created an early space for Indians to pursue science. Its achievements offer valuable lessons for strengthening today’s research landscape in India.

papers.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $χ^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Methods for Generalized Lipschitz Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a convex optimization problem, where the upper bound on the subgradient norm depends on the objective function. We establish a lower bound on the number of iterations required by any first-order method to find an approximate solution to the problem. Furthermore, we present two near-optimal algorithms that can match the lower bound up to logarithmic factors. The first algorithm is a projected GD with a carefully designed stepsize schedule which incorporates warm-up and decay phases. The second algorithm is scalar-stepsize clipped AdamW which extends the near-optimal guarantees to the stochastic setting, where only a noisy unbiased estimator of the subgradient is available.

papers.title: Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters. The resulting analytical hierarchy allows us to distinguish the interplay between both kinds of qubit-qubit interactions and the effects of displacement, neighboring-manifold mixing, and squeezing on the low-energy properties. We find that the transverse interaction mainly changes the collective-spin structure of the states, while the longitudinal interaction also modifies the displacement-dependent oscillator overlaps and introduces an additional two-boson coupling. We compare the analytical results with numerically exact diagonalization for the low-energy spectrum, ground-state energy, mean photon number, two-qubit concurrence, and spin correlations. The results provide a compact analytical description of how direct qubit-qubit interactions modify both the spectrum and the eigenstate structure beyond the rotating-wave approximation for few-qubit light-matter systems.

papers.title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

papers.title: Strengthening Compact Vehicle Routing Formulations through Arc-Flow Aggregation and Refinement
papers.abstract: Arc-flow formulations can provide strong relaxations for mixed-integer program formulations of vehicle routing problems, but the associated networks may be prohibitively large. We study the setting in which multiple arc flow relaxations may be applied, and introduce a dual-guided aggregation and refinement framework that constructs substantially smaller arc-flow formulations while recovering the LP bound of the original networks. Dual information is used both to identify states that can be aggregated without weakening the bound and to guide node disaggregation. We show that the resulting procedure converges finitely to the arc-flow bound of the full arc-flow formulation. The framework retains the original decision variables, allowing cutting planes to be added directly in the original variable space. Moreover, it produces an explicit MILP formulation without relying on column generation or pricing to determine the arc-flow relaxation bound. We apply our approach to the vehicle routing problem with time windows for which we define two arc flow relaxations, as well as two families of cutting planes over the original variable space. Computational experiments show that strong bounds can be obtained using substantially aggregated networks. The resulting root bounds are competitive with those obtained by the branch-and-price solver RouteOpt, while retaining a formulation that can be solved directly by a general-purpose MILP solver.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $ρ\gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(μ_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is \(μ_L\)-stable and \(L\)-Gieseker-stable. The corresponding object \(E_{C,A}^{\vee}[1]\) for \(d<g-1\), or \(E_{C,A}\) for \(d>g-1\), is stable in the adjacent chamber, as its reduction. These results connect dimension estimates for Brill-Noether loci with stability and wall-crossing on abelian surfaces.

papers.title: Hochschild Cocycle and Universality of Merge
papers.abstract: The Hopf algebra Markov chain dynamical system, on the Hopf algebra of non-planar binary forests, that models the action of Merge on workspaces in Chomsky's Minimalist Model of syntax, satisfies a universal property, determined by the fact that the Merge operation is a Hochschild 1-cocycle. This universal property has an interpretation in terms of models of the syntax-semantics interface, as it shows that, if the side of semantics possesses a sufficiently rich compositional structure, then that structure is uniquely induced by the syntactic Merge, once the semantic values of lexical items and syntactic features are assigned. We illustrate how this universality works by showing, in particular, full compatibility of this Hopf algebraic formulation with Heim-Kratzer semantics.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
papers.abstract: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.

papers.title: On cover exacting cardinals
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goldberg about cover exacting cardinals. Concretely, we show that if $κ$ is $ω_1$-strongly compact, then no cardinal $λ>κ$ is $γ$-cover exacting for some cardinal $γ$.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part III: Oracle Complexity of Monotone Variational Inequalities with $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Operators
papers.abstract: We consider monotone variational inequalities in which the Jacobian norm of the operator $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is bounded by an affine function of the norm of the operator itself: $\|DF(z)\|\le L_0+L_1\|F(z)\|$. The main case is the problem on the whole space, that is, finding a zero of $F$. We assume that a solution exists and that an upper bound $R$ on the distance from the starting point to the solution is known. Neither strong monotonicity nor cocoercivity is assumed. Global Lipschitz continuity is not assumed either: for $L_1>0$, the Jacobian norm may grow together with the norm of the operator. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the number of oracle calls sufficient to find a point $\hat z$ with $\|F(\hat z)\|\le\varepsilon$. For $L_0R/\varepsilon\ge1$, both bounds are, up to logarithmic factors in $L_1R$, of order $1+L_0R/\varepsilon+(L_1R)^{6/5}$. The upper bound is attained by a deterministic extragradient-type method, and the lower bound holds for arbitrary randomized methods. The same bounds are obtained for the Minty gap on the ball of radius $R$, where $L_0R/\varepsilon$ is replaced by $L_0R^2/η$. In addition, we show that for a variational inequality on a bounded set the numbers $L_0,L_1$ and the diameter of the set are not sufficient: a uniform complexity bound requires additional information, for example, an upper bound on the norm of the operator at the solution.

papers.title: Covariance Cells And Star Products
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, a localized preparation is described not only by a point in phase space but also by a covariance cell specifying its finite resolution. We study balanced Gaussian cells on a linear symplectic space and show that they are equivalent to compatible complex structures and positive Lagrangian polarizations. Their parameter space is the Siegel symmetric space. Using the Koopman-von Neumann representation of classical mechanics, we describe the linearized transport of Gaussian amplitudes along a reference motion. Each covariance cell determines a separated star product whose antisymmetric part is fixed by the symplectic form and whose symmetric part is fixed by the covariance. This product is related to the Moyal product by Gaussian smoothing. Quadratic Hamiltonians act through their classical Poisson derivations within a fixed cell algebra exactly when they preserve the cell; squeezing transformations instead relate the algebras associated with different cells. Fronsdal's star-polarization construction yields a module whose cyclic element is the Gaussian density of the cell. Its completion is the corresponding Bargmann-Fock space, naturally embedded in the space of classical Koopman amplitudes. Koopman transport carries this Fock space to that of the transported cell. No Planck constant is introduced: the deformation parameter is a classical resolution scale, and physical observables remain commuting multiplication operators.

papers.title: Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, let $T\subseteq V$, and let $F\subseteq E$. We call $F$ semi-cutting for $T$ if $d_{G}(u,w)<d_{G\setminus F}(u,w)$ for every two distinct terminals $u,w\in T$. We prove the sharp bound $|F|\ge |T|-1$. The argument is structural: semi-cutting sets are first identified with edge transversals of all shortest terminal-terminal paths, and the bound then follows from a contraction step, a terminal-deletion lemma, and a lexicographic induction on $(|T|,|V|)$.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $η\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $η$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $η=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
papers.abstract: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific. Maternal and Perinatal Health scored lowest (28.0%), followed by Dental and Oral Health (38.5%) and Behavioral Health (44.4%), while Long-Term Services and Supports (82.8%) and Experience of Care (67.8%) scored highest. State performance correlated strongly with national benchmarks (r = 0.77, approximately), so rates should be read against each measure's benchmark. Domain was the strongest predictor, and the model explained 31.2% of variance. Because of heteroscedasticity and influential observations from mixing bounded and utilization measures, estimates are descriptive. Quality improvement should be targeted by domain, prioritizing maternal health, behavioral health network adequacy, and dental provider participation.

papers.title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown $m$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{M}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is $F=f\circΠ_{\mathcal{M}}$, where $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the nearest-point projection onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $f:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}^p$ is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For $p\ge m$, under our geometric and sampling conditions, $n$ independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order $n^{-2/(m+4)}$ and integrated squared prediction error at the $m$-dimensional nonparametric rate $n^{-4/(m+4)}$, up to logarithmic factors. In a scaling regime with fixed intrinsic dimension, model and scale parameters, and ratio of manifold volume to the $m$-th power of its reach, the required sample size grows polynomially in $D+p$, and computation is polynomial in $n$, $D$ and $p$. Numerical experiments on curves with non-monotone links and surfaces with vector-valued responses compare observed convergence rates with the theoretical bounds; a Langevin dynamics example tests prediction of hitting probabilities under an approximate manifold-index model.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, I: the mass matrix and the polygon model
papers.abstract: A canonical metric $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ on $S^n \setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$, where $\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}=(p_1,\ldots,p_{\ell})$ and $n \ge 3$, is a metric conformal to the round metric that is complete, scalar-flat, and asymptotically flat at each puncture $p_i$. For $n=3$ these metrics are the Brill--Lindquist time-symmetric initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and their ends carry ADM masses. In this paper we study the masses, through the mass matrix, as functions on the conformal moduli space $M_{\ell}(S^n)$. The mass matrix $η=(η_{ij})$ is a symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and vanishing row sums (these matrices form the space $H_{\ell}$), and it determines the \emph{normalized ADM mass} at the $i$-th end via $\hat{\mathfrak{m}}_i=\sum_{j\ne i}e^{η_{ij}}$. We prove that the mass map $Ξ\colon M_\ell(S^n)\to H_{\ell}$ is a homeomorphism onto its image. On the other hand, the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_\ell(S^n)$ is homeomorphic to the moduli space of those equilateral $\ell$-gons in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$ whose sides, extended to infinity, end at distinct points (the Gauss map). By a theorem of Kapovich--Leeb--Millson and Balser, every polystable configuration is the Gauss image of such a polygon, and the Gauss map identifies the space of all equilateral $\ell$-gons with a natural compactification of $M_\ell(S^n)$. In particular, the mass matrix has an explicit description in terms of the pairwise vertex distances of the polygon. The mass matrix diverges as punctures collide. The degeneration, its renormalization, and the resulting compactification of the moduli space are the subject of a sequel to this paper.

papers.title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

papers.title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{ω^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
papers.abstract: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by Itô stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path. Each notion is characterized by a differential condition that is necessary and sufficient for contraction under mild hypotheses. Relations between contraction notions and an associated incremental input-to-state stability result are also established. As an illustration, we apply the established theory to analyze noise-induced synchronization and quantify its robustness with respect to parameter perturbations.

papers.title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

papers.title: Asymptotic radial symmetry of $p$-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers on the disk
papers.abstract: We solve the minimizer case of Brezis's Open Problem~2.3 for every fixed $p>2$. For $\varepsilon>0$, let $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}\in W^{1,p}(B_1;\mathbb{R}^2)$ be a global minimizer of the $p$-Ginzburg--Landau energy \[ \int_{B_1} \left( \frac{|\nabla\mathbf{u}|^p}{p} +\frac{(1-|\mathbf{u}|^2)^2}{4\varepsilon^2} \right)\,dx \] with prescribed trace $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}|_{\partial B_1}(x)=x$. We prove that, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}(x)\to x/|x|$ at every point $x\in B_1\setminus\{0\}$. The convergence is strong in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_1\setminus\{0\};\mathbb{R}^2)$ and hence uniform on every compact subset of the punctured disk. On each such compact subset, the potential energy tends to zero and the total energy converges to the $p$-Dirichlet energy of the radial map. No symmetry or uniqueness of the minimizers is assumed. The proof combines whole-plane concentration, a strict exterior filling estimate, and quantitative convexity to locate the concentration point and identify the limiting map.

papers.title: Uniform compactness in a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems
papers.abstract: In their paper on non-coercive boundary value problems, Kohn and Nirenberg show that a priori estimates for all forms satisfying $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann boundary conditions follow from a compactness estimate. Inspired by Hamilton, we show that these a priori estimates are stable under deformations of the complex structure, the hermitian metric and the volume form of the underlying manifold. We use a parameter $m$ to encode a deformation of this data. We show that if a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems depends smoothly on $m$ and the compactness estimate(s) hold (with constants uniform in $m$), then the family of solution operators also depends smoothly $m$. As a consequence we obtain sufficient conditions for the Bergman kernel to vary smoothly in a family of domains. We also provide a sufficient condition for the uniform compactness estimate(s) to hold in a family of domains.

papers.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1970 Monsky showed that a square cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles. His proof used an ingenious colouring of the plane based on a 2-adic valuation on $\mathbb{R}$ together with Sperner's lemma. Subsequent work established similar results for regular polygons, centrally symmetric polygons, and polyominoes. In 2000, Stein proposed a common generalisation of the centrally symmetric and polyomino cases to balanced polygons. In 2014, Rudenko introduced a new perspective on the problem and proved Stein's conjecture for dissections with rational vertex coordinates. Building on and streamlining his approach, we resolve the conjecture in full.

papers.title: Torsion phenomena in symplectic capacities via Clarke duality
papers.abstract: We study Gutt--Hutchings capacities with finite cyclic coefficients and show that torsion in positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology detects new obstructions to symplectic embeddings between convex toric domains. Prime-field coefficients give no additional obstructions in this class, while the torsion responsible for the new obstructions already appears over $\mathbb Z/p^{p+2}$ for every prime $p$. We prove a stabilization theorem for these capacities on convex bodies with arbitrary commutative coefficients, yielding a sharp stabilized embedding obstruction in an explicit example. Clarke duality makes these phenomena accessible to computation. We extend the filtered equivariant Clarke--Floer comparison to arbitrary commutative coefficient rings and compute the capacities using models of dual action sublevels built from representation spheres. The circle-action weights encode orbit covering multiplicities, whose products govern the new obstructions.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ be an irreducible properly convex projective domain admitting a discrete cocompact group action of projective automorphisms. We prove that the Holmes--Thompson volumes of projective simplices with vertices in $Ω$ are uniformly bounded. As a consequence, we prove that a closed properly convex projective manifold of dimension at least two has positive simplicial volume if and only if it is irreducible.

papers.title: Local Limit Theorems and Edgeworth Expansions for some classes of inhomogeneous Markov chains
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove local central limit theorems and expansions in the central limit theorem for inhomogeneous Markov chains satisfying a one-step lower ellipticity condition. As for the local limit theorem, in the general inhomogeneous case, compared with \cite{DS}, we are able to prove results without two-sided ellipticity, although only in the one-step case. Compared with \cite{PeligradLLT1,PeligradLLT2}, we are able to prove local limit theorems without a lower $ψ$-mixing condition. Concerning Edgeworth expansions, compared with \cite{DHPTRF1}, we are able to get results without two-sided ellipticity (under some sequential Diophantine conditions). Our conditions are then verified for Markov chains in a random dynamical environment with a one-sided Doeblin condition under very mild assumptions. For Markov chains in a random environment, we also consider the more general case of $φ$-mixing chains and then, under some mild periodicity assumptions on the environment, we prove local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions (without any ellipticity assumptions), matching the results for deterministic homogeneous chains. When the chain is driven by a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, we obtain high-order expansions for $φ$-mixing chains under some Diophantine conditions of a deterministic system generated by a periodic point. We then apply our results to bounded additive functionals of posterior states in disordered quantum trajectories and establish local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions.

papers.title: Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
papers.abstract: We study approximate $K$-conjugacy for minimal Cantor--circle extensions with arbitrary circle homeomorphism cocycles, allowing orientation reversal. Under the assumption of classical rigidity, we show that two such systems are approximately $K$-conjugate if and only if there exists an ordered unital graded $K$-theory isomorphism satisfying the finite coefficient $K$-condition. Our approach combines dynamical corrections along Kakutani--Rokhlin towers with the classification and uniqueness theory of $C^*$-algebras. Moreover, the crossed-product isomorphisms implementing approximate $K$-conjugacy can be chosen as inner perturbations of a fixed isomorphism and its inverse.

papers.title: $p$-ellipticity for systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients
papers.abstract: We extend the concept of $p$-ellipticity for (single) elliptic operators, that we introduced in arxiv:1611.00653, to the case of systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients. The $p$-ellipticity condition from this paper turns out to be equivalent, up to a factor depending on $p$, to a condition for systems introduced (and equally named) by Dindoš, Li and Pipher in arXiv:2007.13190. We prove several key properties of $p$-ellipticity akin to those that have been known to hold in the scalar case (arxiv:1611.00653). In some respects, however, the vector case fundamentally differs from the scalar one. As an application we establish the contractivity on $L^p$ of the operator semigroup generated by systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients and subject to Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.

papers.title: Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
papers.abstract: We consider a system of Stochastic Differential Equations with two time scales, so called slow-fast system of SDEs. As customary when studying slow-fast dynamics, we seek a coarse grained description of the system, obtained, in the limit of scale separation, by 'averaging out' the fast component of the dynamics (so-called averaging limit). We study slow-fast systems where the fast variable is described by a process which is non-linear in the sense of McKean i.e. by an SDE whose coefficients depend on the law of the process itself, while the slow variable is a linear SDE (linear in the sense of McKean). We show that, when the fast variable is a McKean-Vlasov process and, additionally, the coefficients of the SDE depend on the position of the slow process, the limit of scale separation is not provided by the usual ansatz which one would expect by applying classical averaging paradigms. We identify the limit and provide complete proof.

papers.title: feedback-grape: A JAX-based Python Package for GPU-Accelerated GRAPE with Feedback
papers.abstract: Modern quantum technology applications require accurate control of quantum systems, including a feedback loop in the control process. While open-loop control can be performed using well established gradient methods like GRadient Ascent Pulse Engineering (GRAPE), it was until recently unclear how to combine these with feedback from measurements, which are inherently non-differentiable. Recent work has successfully demonstrated how feedback can be incorporated into GRAPE using machine learning, resolving this issue. Following this progress, we have developed an efficient Python package implementing the method of ``feedback GRAPE''. In this hands-on tutorial, we discuss the package in detail based on concrete examples. Built on the GPU-accelerated JAX platform, our package offers a user-friendly interface inspired by the widely-used QuTiP library, including simplified treatment of multi-component systems.

papers.title: Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
papers.abstract: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $π_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[ π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\frac{d_1+\cdots+d_k}{\logλ_\mathbf{d}}\,\log N, \] where $λ_\mathbf{d}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $M(d_1)\cdots M(d_k)$. For the Fibonacci word this gives $π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\log N/\log\varphi$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$.

papers.title: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
papers.abstract: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

papers.title: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
papers.abstract: Let $E_n$ be $α_n$-uniformly perfect compact sets that converge to a compact set $E$ in the Hausdorff distance $d_n=d_H(E_n,E)$. We prove that the logarithmic capacity of $E_n$ converges to that of $E$ whenever $\log(1/α_n)=O(\log(1/d_n))$ and that no factor tending to infinity can be inserted in this bound. A common energy-transfer theorem also yields Hausdorff continuity of Riesz capacity under local capacity bounds, including bounds obtained from lower Hausdorff content density. Finally, we correct our earlier claims about the uniform convergence of Green functions.

papers.title: Decorated lattices: hyperuniformity and limit theorems
papers.abstract: We introduce \emph{decorated lattices}, a point process obtained by placing finite random point configurations in lattice cells. A stationary mark field selects the motif laws and acts as a random environment transmitting dependence between cells, while allowing flexible local arrangements. Using this construction, one can efficiently generate large regions of disordered patterns with desired local behavior while the random environment controls the asymptotic density fluctuations. Under moment and summability assumptions, we derive an explicit decomposition of the Bartlett spectral measure into contributions from conditional motif fluctuations and correlations between marks. This yields criteria for hyperuniformity, or generally $p$-uniformity. Independent, nondegenerate count fluctuations destroy hyperuniformity, whereas suitable dependence governed by the random environment can restore it despite random and unequal cell counts. Once count fluctuations are sufficiently suppressed, motif geometry and its spatial correlations govern the finer order of uniformity. Under mixing assumptions, we also establish central limit theorems for linear statistics, with fluctuations governed by cell counts or, at a finer scale, by the first spatial moments of the motifs.

papers.title: Counterfactual Screening of Rare Secondary Overloads in Power Grids with a Stochastic Surrogate for Electromagnetic Transient Simulations
papers.abstract: Power-system operators continually ask what would happen if a component failed now. Single-phase-to-ground faults cleared by single-pole tripping and automatic reclosure usually have no lasting consequences. In rare cases, however, the transient excited during the open-phase interval drives distant lines or transformers into overload that persists after the faulted line is restored. We develop a counterfactual screening framework for these secondary overloads, combining a linear stochastic swing surrogate with cross-entropy importance sampling. The surrogate represents the open-phase corridor through an effective coupling factor and localized multiplicative noise, with both parameters learned from electromagnetic-transient (EMT) simulations rather than prescribed. Closed-form propagation of the mean and covariance permits deterministic calibration without Monte Carlo sampling. On the reduced WECC 240-bus system, a globally calibrated model substantially improves finite-time agreement with the EMT electromechanical state. The global models are calibrated at reclosure and tested on disjoint faulted lines under a longer open-phase interval. Line- and operating-state-specific models use additional reclosure data from the assessment lines and provide smaller further gains at the cost of more separate fits. The fitted coupling is lower than the phase-counting baseline, consistent with the direction anticipated by sequence-network analysis. Cross-entropy importance sampling directs computational effort toward contingencies associated with persistent overload and yields rare-event probability estimates together with a map linking initiating faults to the elements they endanger. By separating offline EMT calibration from repeated surrogate evaluation, the method supports probabilistic contingency screening and identifies where detailed high-fidelity assessment is most valuable.

papers.title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
papers.abstract: We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

papers.title: Independent set reconfiguration is hard at treewidth four
papers.abstract: Independent Set Reconfiguration asks whether one of two given independent sets of equal size can be transformed into the other by moving one token at a time while keeping the occupied vertices independent. In token sliding, a token moves along an edge. In token jumping, it may move to any unoccupied vertex. For both rules, the problem is solvable in polynomial time on trees and is PSPACE-complete on graphs of treewidth at most $c$ for some fixed constant $c$. For each rule, the smallest treewidth bound that suffices for hardness has long been open. We narrow this gap by proving that both versions are NP-hard on graphs of treewidth four.

papers.title: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit. We further show that the balance identity behind the theorem singles out quadratic feedback: a $q$-Gaussian with $q<2$ satisfies it only for a quadratic conditional variance, and no $q$-Gaussian with $2\le q<3$ satisfies it for any conditional variance. The proofs use the method of moments for negative feedback and a Wasserstein coupling argument for positive feedback, including cases in which the limiting variance is infinite.

papers.title: Learning Advantage Function Surrogates via Convex Conjugate Matching
papers.abstract: A policy trained to make per-unit decisions, such as how much of a product to order, tells us the best action but not the cost of deviating from it. That cost, the advantage function, is what downstream systems need when they have to depart from the per-unit optimum: to estimate the impact of ordering more or fewer units, to respond to a one-off vendor discount, or to satisfy a shared capacity constraint. The advantage function is what makes such trade-offs computable, yet pure policy-learning algorithms often produce the policy alone, without a critic that would yield it. We propose a method to train an advantage function surrogate through price perturbations motivated by a Fenchel-Young loss. We describe a two-stage recipe (fit the policy, then the cost model) and illustrate it on a multi-period inventory management problem.

papers.title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
papers.abstract: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$. For $m\in\{2,3,4\}$ we construct integral identities at length $L(t)=m(t+3)-2$ over $C_m^3$, and prove that these thresholds are sharp over fields of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing $m$. For a prime $p\nmid m$ and $0\le a\le b\le c$, we prove that \[ D(C_{mp^a}\oplus C_{mp^b}\oplus C_{mp^c}) =m(p^a+p^b+p^c)-2. \] In particular $D(C_{15}^3)=43$ and $D(C_{20}^3)=58$, which are the two smallest cases of the conjecture $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ left open in the literature. The proofs of the base cases for $m \in \{3,4\}$ are computer-assisted. All of the results in this paper have been formalised in Lean 4.

papers.title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations.
