The present scheme generates the time-periodic Gibbs state as if a limit-cycle solution of the innovated GKSL equation under the time-periodic driving field. Thanks to the FF variant of DBC, we see the energy conservation of power and heat current of the system, and reversibility of whole system including a reservoir. The requirement of positivity of the FF dissipative coefficients imposes a constraint on the speed of the FF driving. At low temperature, the upper speed limit of the FF periodic driving is found to be proportional to $\tildeβ^{-1/2}\exp(a\tildeβ)$ with $\tildeβ$ the scaled inverse temperature and $a$ the positive constant of $O(1)$.

papers.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
papers.abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.

papers.title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
papers.abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_xΦ(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.

papers.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $φ^4_2$ fields
papers.abstract: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.

papers.title: Online Carbon-Aware Power Flexibility Quantification of Distributed Data Centers
papers.abstract: Geographically distributed data centers (DCs) can provide spatio-temporal power flexibility to electric grids through the coordinated management of computing resources and energy. Beyond their energy consumption, the carbon footprints of DCs are non-negligible, which constrain the power flexibility that DCs can offer to the power grid. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a carbon-aware power flexibility quantification framework for DCs. We first develop an optimization model that characterizes DC power flexibility in a grid-usable form, namely the Cartesian product of adjustable power demand intervals across time slots. An online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization is then designed to solve the flexibility quantification model in real time under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity. Furthermore, an integrated disaggregation and feedback mechanism is devised to translate the power system operator's dispatch commands into real-time DC operating decisions and to capture their impact on future DC flexibility. Several desirable properties of the proposed model and method are proven, including disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our approach effectively unlocks DC power flexibility while satisfying carbon emission constraints, outperforming baseline algorithms.

papers.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

papers.title: General linear groups in tangent categories
papers.abstract: General linear groups are well-studied Lie groups that encode the linear symmetries of a finitely-dimensional linear space. In differential geometry, they are an important ingredient of various constructions, including fibre bundles and the frame bundle of a principal bundle. They also appear in algebraic geometry as affine group schemes. Their Lie algebra, known as the general linear Lie algebra, is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of square matrices, whose Lie bracket is given by the commutator. Building on previous work on Lie groups, in this paper we introduce general linear group objects in the context of tangent categories. We define the general linear group of a differential object as a classifier of the Kleisli parametrized linear automorphisms of the differential object, a class of maps that generalize linear automorphisms in a suitable sense. We prove that such a group can be entirely constructed via a tangent triple equalizer and use this characterization to prove that the Lie algebra of general linear group objects is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of linear endomorphisms.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for First- and Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods for Planar Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{ü}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Numerical verification for harmonic maps: Counterexamples to Eells' conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper develops a framework to construct harmonic maps $S^3 \rightarrow S^2$ numerically, which is used to construct approximate harmonic maps in homotopy classes with Hopf invariant $2,3,4,5,6$. By using a rigorous fixed-point argument, it is shown that there exist genuine harmonic maps with the same Hopf invariant close to these approximate solutions, thus producing a family of counterexamples to Eells' conjecture, and the related Ding's conjecture.

papers.title: Admissible Yang--Baxter equation for Nijenhuis perm superalgebras
papers.abstract: We develop a superization of the theory of admissible Yang--Baxter equations for Nijenhuis perm algebras initiated by Ma and Song. We introduce Nijenhuis perm superalgebras, their representations, and the dual representation, with Koszul signs chosen so that the contraction of the Yang--Baxter tensor matches the $\mathcal O$-operator equation exactly. We define Nijenhuis perm superbialgebras and characterise them by matched pairs. In the coboundary case, we show that every even supersymmetric solution of the $S$-admissible perm Yang--Baxter equation gives rise to a Nijenhuis perm superbialgebra, and we give sufficient conditions for a perm superalgebra to admit a Nijenhuis operator constructed from such a solution. Examples with purely odd components illustrate the role of the grading.

papers.title: Co-rotating and traveling asymmetric vortex sheets for the planar Euler equation
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to construct co-rotating and traveling vortex sheet pairs with asymmetric configurations for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation. The vorticity of these solutions is concentrated on two small closed curves of different sizes, which carry vortex sheets of different circulations and either rotate uniformly about their centroid or translate with constant speed. The proof relies on the Birkhoff--Rott formulation of the problem and on the implicit function theorem at the point vortex pairs.

papers.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.

papers.title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

papers.title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
papers.abstract: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transport robots, an agent-written solver improved seven of ten MKT instances. New lower bounds show that four published MKT values cannot be attained on the distributed instance files. Agent-run improvement campaigns closed eight further instances.

papers.title: Nonexistence of a quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design
papers.abstract: It is shown that there exists no quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design with intersection numbers $6$ and $9$. This is proved by considering the ternary code generated by the incidence vectors of the blocks and its dual code.

papers.title: Folding of cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary symmetrizable Cartan data and arbitrary positive braids, we prove that the Laurent homomorphism identifying corresponding seed variables restricts to a surjective algebra homomorphism between the corresponding cluster algebras. We also extend the Kimura--Oya quantum twist automorphisms to arbitrary positive braids after localization at the frozen variables, and prove that their commutative specializations commute with the folding homomorphisms.

papers.title: Strong solutions to the Cahn--Hilliard--Darcy--Forchheimer system for incompressible two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant
papers.abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for incompressible viscous two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant in a bounded porous medium in two or three dimensions. The resulting system consists of a Darcy--Forchheimer equation for the seepage velocity $\bm{u}$ coupled with two Cahn--Hilliard equations, one for the difference in volume fractions of the two fluids denoted by $φ$, and the other for the local concentration of the surfactant $ψ$. In the general scenario of non-constant coefficients and mobilities, we establish the existence of a local (resp. global) strong solution in three (resp. two) dimensions to the corresponding initial-boundary value problem with the no-flux boundary conditions for the phase-field variables and chemical potentials and a no-penetration condition for the velocity. In the case of constant coefficients in the Darcy--Forchheimer equation and constant mobilities in the Cahn--Hilliard equations, with a suitably large Forchheimer exponent, we establish the existence of a global strong solution in three dimensions. Furthermore, using the Łojasiewicz--Simon approach, we prove the global existence of a unique strong solution when the initial data are sufficiently close to a local energy minimizer of the free energy.

papers.title: The elephant random walk with proportionally growing recent memory
papers.abstract: In this work, we study an elephant random walk with recent restricted memory, where at step $n$ the elephant remembers only the last $m_n=\max\{\lfloor cn\rfloor,1\}$ steps for $c\in(0,1)$. We show that the random walk undergoes a phase transition at the critical point $p_c=(3+\sqrt{1-c})/4$, which depends on the memory proportion $c$. For $0<p<p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n}$ is asymptotically normal; for $p=p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ is asymptotically normal; and for $p_c<p<1$, $S_n/n^ρ$ converges almost surely and in $L^2$ to a random variable for some constant $ρ\in (1/2, 1)$. This phase transition differs from that of the classical elephant random walk and its remote-memory counterpart, both of which have the same fixed critical point $3/4$.

papers.title: Schreier Sets And the Product of Fibonacci And Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: First, we introduce strictly super-Schreier sets, which provide a new combinatorial interpretation of products of Fibonacci and Catalan numbers. Second, we show that the numbers of sets in higher-order Schreier families do not satisfy any linear recurrence relation, thus answering a question in the existing literature.

papers.title: Optimal Dividend Problem for a Threshold Dependent Surplus Process with Bounded Dividend Rate
papers.abstract: We study optimal bounded-rate dividend payments for a diffusion surplus process whose drift and volatility change at a fixed surplus threshold. Optimal strategies admit an exhaustive classification into zero-threshold, positive single-threshold, two-boundary, and three-boundary configurations. The latter two configurations have separated dividend regions, which arise because the interface can reverse the monotonicity of the derivative of the value function with respect to the initial surplus. Multiband optimality requires an upward change in drift. Without prescribing a strategy in advance, we construct the unique bounded classical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman transmission problem by varying the derivative at zero surplus and selecting the unique value for which the resulting solution agrees in both value and derivative with a bounded solution at a fixed sufficiently large surplus level. Verification identifies this solution with the value function and determines the optimal feedback strategy. For each configuration, we derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and characterize the switching boundaries through explicit formulas or equations in one unknown obtained by matching the value function and its derivative. The analysis also shows how changes in the drift and volatility of the upper regime affect the optimal value and dividend strategy. Numerical analysis illustrates how model parameters affect the optimal dividend regions.

papers.title: Geometric Partial Differential Equations of Hydrodynamic Type for Maps into F$_\text{man}$-Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric framework for partial differential equations of hydrodynamic type on maps from a two-dimensional manifold into an F$_\text{man}$-Lie group. Using the left-invariant structure and the Maurer-Cartan form, we reduce these equations to non-linear evolution systems on the underlying F$_\text{man}$-algebra, governed by its Lie bracket and commutative associative product. We investigate the role of Poisson subalgebras, establishing that flatness of the canonical connection forces two-step nilpotency and yields a linearized evolution equation upon quotienting by the center. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a Poisson splitting and derive the corresponding tangential and transversal evolution equations. Under suitable reductivity assumptions, we show that their non-linear coupling is governed by the curvature of the canonical principal connection on the homogeneous space $G/H$. These results reveal the interplay between the algebraic structure of F$_\text{man}$-Lie groups and the geometric dynamics of hydrodynamic-type equations.

papers.title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a $50\times50$ array in 12.5 $μ$s. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a $35\times35$ target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 $μ$s for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a $[[1122,148]]$ lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 $μ$s with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

papers.title: Vector bundles on spin Kähler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
papers.abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin Kähler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.

papers.title: A large ultrafilter number at $\aleph_ω$
papers.abstract: Gitik constructed a model where $\aleph_ω$ is strong limit, $2^{\aleph_ω}=\aleph_{ω+2}$ and every strongly uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$. We show that in fact every uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$ in that model.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
papers.abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.

papers.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a unital \(σ\)-weakly closed subalgebra \(\mathfrak A\) of a von Neumann factor \(\mathcal M\) of type \(\mathrm{II}_1\), whose diagonal is \(\mathfrak D=\mathfrak A\cap\mathfrak A^*=\mathbb CI\). We show that there exist uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations from \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\mathfrak D\) with respect to each of which \(\mathfrak A\) is a maximal subdiagonal algebra. Let \(τ\) denote the unique normalized faithful normal trace on \(\mathcal M\). The conditional expectation associated with \(τ\) preserves this trace, whereas none of the other conditional expectations is preserved by any nonzero finite trace on \(\mathcal M\). This gives a negative answer to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras in \emph{Amer. J. Math.} \textbf{89}(1967), 578--642.

papers.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
papers.abstract: We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $Γ/ν$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{\rm adv}(Γ/ν)^{s}$, the vorticity $ω_θ$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{νt})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and Šverák \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.

papers.title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
papers.abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Liénard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.

papers.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
papers.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

papers.title: The Gaps Between the $Δ$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $u^Δ(K)$ denote the $Δ$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^Δ(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $Δ$-gap of $K$ by $G^Δ(K):=u^Δ(K)-|a_2(K)|$. In this paper, we investigate the behavior of this invariant for various families of knots. For example, we prove that the $Δ$-gap of the pretzel knot $K=P(2s, 4s-1,4s+1)$, where $s$ is a positive integer, satisfies $G^Δ(K) \geq 4s$. Consequently, the $Δ$-gap is unbounded. To further investigate the structure of the $Δ$-gap, we distinguish between $Δ$-moves that increase $a_2(K)$ and those that decrease it, since each $Δ$-move changes $a_2(K)$ by $\pm1$. We analyze how these two types of moves contribute to the $Δ$-gap. We also investigate the gaps between $u^Δ(K)$ and other knot invariants that provide lower bounds for it. In particular, we establish explicit formulas and lower bounds for these gaps for certain families of pretzel knots, torus knots, two-bridge knots, and Montesinos knots. Our results show that these gaps can be arbitrarily large. In addition, we identify prime positive knots with $u^Δ(K)=2$ or $3$, and propose a conjecture on a lower bound for $u^Δ(K)$ for prime positive knots.

papers.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

papers.title: Innovative Integrated Congestion Management Market: Synergizing Operational Flexibility of Transmission System Operators with Aggregator-Driven Resources
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an innovative congestion management market that seeks to integrate and harness the operational flexibility available to Transmission System Operators (TSO) in conjunction with the flexibility offered by aggregators. In the context of operational flexibility, this study investigates Network Topology Optimization (NTO) as a pivotal strategy for to address the transmission network congestion, specifically through the strategic switching of certain buses. To achieve this, an N-1 secured NTO is formulated using a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) methodology. Concurrently, acknowledging the crucial and growing importance of aggregator-provided flexibility in congestion management, the paper presents a novel integrated congestion management market. In this framework, aggregators submit bids, and the TSO, taking into account these bids alongside the potential for the NTO, clears the market with the goal of minimizing the overall cost of congestion management. The proposed integrated market is constructed using a linear optimization model, ensuring its practical applicability in real world scenarios. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed market design are assessed using the standard IEEE 39-bus system, with results indicating promising potential and applicability

papers.title: Pseudo-profiles for vectorial Allen-Cahn systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to present a new type of solutions to the elliptic vectorial Allen-Cahn system of equations. Its main feature is that in the classical rescaling its asymptotics do not follow the rule of balance of energies, which is crucial in the analysis of the asymptotics for the scalar problem.

papers.title: Homogeneous pursuit in $β$ model
papers.abstract: Data in forms of networks has been encountered in various prevalent fields at the arrival of big data era. To unveil and recover the true model with core units with numerous links, the $β$-model under sparsity constraint is proposed to meet the expectation of statisticians and engineers. Not only does this network model inherit spectacular property from the Erdős-Rényi model, but also exhibits degree heterogeneity through tuning sparsity parameter $s$. In this paper, we propose Homogeneous Pursuit (HP), an $\ell_0$-constrained maximum likelihood estimation method implemented through a primal-dual algorithm. To ease the harshness of computation, we find the surrogate function of the corresponding objective function to derive Majorization Minimization algorithm through the primal-dual process. Moreover, after meticulous evaluation, the algorithm brought about captures the property of fine convergence rate in a contraction mapping way. Under some mild conditions, the proposed generalized information criterion (GIC$^*$) for selecting the sparsity level is consistent to find the truth. Combining HP with GIC$^*$ gives the adaptive procedure HP-GIC$^*$; HP-BIC denotes the same estimation method with sparsity selected by BIC. Finally, simulation studies show that GIC$^*$ improves support recovery relative to BIC in the reported comparisons, while HP achieves lower computational cost while maintaining estimation accuracy comparable to the sparse benchmark methods. A microfinance application illustrates the use of HP-GIC$^*$ for studying the association between network prominence and participation, with improved fit in the reported village-level regressions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
papers.abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.

papers.title: Just publish it
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03524-9Just publish it

papers.title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
papers.abstract: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers. First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$. Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$. The new ingredient is an explicit robber strategy showing that two cops do not suffice on $\mathrm{GP}(3k,k)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(4k,k)$ for $k\geq 4$. The theorem on flower snarks and all of the new lower bounds have been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4π$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current.

papers.title: Homotopy type of equivariant embeddings
papers.abstract: We study spaces of symplectic embeddings of a closed four-ball into a closed symplectic four-manifold that are equivariant under a compact group action and centred on a component of the fixed point set. Adapting McDuff's argument, we reduce the path-connectedness of these spaces, and the uniqueness of equivariant blow-ups up to isotopy, to an equivariant deformation-to-isotopy statement on the blow-up. For compact abelian groups, we identify the stabilizer of a ball with the group of equivariant symplectomorphisms of the blow-up that preserve the exceptional divisor. For Hamiltonian circle actions on $\mathbb{C}P^2$, $S^2\times S^2$ and $\mathbb{C}P^2\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$, we obtain the invariant curves needed for inflation from toric extensions of the blown-up action, and we prove that the embedding spaces are path-connected. When the ball is centred at an isolated fixed point of $S^2\times S^2$ or $\mathbb{C}P^2\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$, the space of unparametrized balls is contractible or homotopy equivalent to $ΩS^3\times S^1$, according to the numbers of toric actions that extend the circle action and its blow-up. On $\mathbb{C}P^2$, it is homotopy equivalent to the fixed component. Along the way, we compute the centralizers of Hamiltonian circle actions on the one-point blow-up of $S^2\times S^2$, whose homotopy type depends only on the number of toric extensions.

papers.title: Scattering for cubic and Yukawa--Hartree Dirac equations wiith polynomially decaying spacetime metrics
papers.abstract: We study massive Dirac equations in three space dimensions with small, time-dependent perturbations of the principal coefficients and decaying zeroth-order matrix terms. The principal perturbation and its spatial derivatives decay polynomially at rate $ρ>7/2$, and its first time derivative has one additional inverse spatial power. We prove small-data global well-posedness and scattering for local cubic nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1+5/(2(ρ-1))$, and for Yukawa--Hartree nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1/2+5/(2(ρ-1))$. The argument retains the coupling between the metric-adapted positive and negative branches. Its main ingredients are a time-independent modified energy, a weighted estimate controlling the full massive low-frequency component, and frequency-dependent spatial cutoffs. The operator class contains the geometric Dirac Hamiltonian of a synchronous spacetime metric with its full spin connection. No second time derivative, temporal integrability, or asymptotic stationarity is assumed. Scattering is formulated relative to the exact nonautonomous linear evolution.

papers.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
papers.abstract: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.

papers.title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
papers.abstract: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.

papers.title: Commuting pairs in lattices of reductive Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We count ordered commuting pairs in a full lattice \(Λ\) in a reductive Lie algebra \(\g\) over \(\Q\). For a fixed convex body \(B\) containing the origin in its interior, the count in \(HB\) is \(C_{Λ,B}H^{\dim\g+\dim Z(\g)}\) with a power-saving error. The leading term comes from pairs whose projections to each simple ideal are linearly dependent over its centroid. Their slopes index an absolutely convergent sum of section volumes for \(C_{Λ,B}\). Subtracting the contribution of dependent pairs from the finite-field Fourier sums gives cancellation at generic dependent frequencies. For independent frequencies, we bound the dimension of the locus where the corresponding hyperplane contains an irreducible component of a nonzero bracket fibre. For \(n\ge3\), the number of ordered commuting pairs in \(M_n(\Z)\) with entries of absolute value at most \(H\) is \[ \frac{2(n+3)ζ(n^2-2)}{(n+1)ζ(n^2-1)} (2\lfloor H\rfloor+1)^{n^2+1} +O_n\!\left(H^{n^2+1-1/(n+1)}\right), \] confirming the exponent \(n^2+1\) predicted by Browning, Sawin and Wang~\cite{BSW}.

papers.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

papers.title: DRAG-Inspired Single Flux Quantum Control of Superconducting Qubits
papers.abstract: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control based on Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) digital electronics is presented. For transmon qubits, optimized control sequences are constructed from regular pulse trains framed by arbitrary subsequences (ramps), enabling DRAG-inspired leakage suppression in the discrete SFQ regime through genetic-algorithm optimization. For representative $Y_{π/2}$ gates, the resulting sequences achieve simulated coherent-control infidelities below $10^{-4}$, including leakage from the computational subspace. The objective of the proposed approach is to demonstrate that coherent errors intrinsic to SFQ control can be reduced to a comparable level for a more scalable cryogenic control architecture. Memory requirements are reduced by storing only the optimized ramps, while a modular controller architecture supporting both regular and arbitrary pulse generation is proposed. The logical complexity of this architecture is estimated from the Josephson-junction counts of its constituent SFQ cells. The proposed approach therefore combines low coherent-control error with reduced memory overhead and provides a basis for scalable cryogenic SFQ control architectures.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.

papers.title: Red-Blue Hamiltonian Tomography via the Operator Lightcone Wavemap
papers.abstract: We introduce a model-free method for Hamiltonian tomography based on the operator spreading wavefront. Given two tensor network simulations of the same quantum lattice (one with the nominal Hamiltonian and one with one or more perturbed bonds), the signed cross-entropy of the non-identity Pauli weight field $\mathcal{L}(v,t) = -\ln(n_{\rm pert}/n_{\rm base})$ identifies each perturbed bond by its causal signature: a red-blue sign flip at the two endpoints, visible from the first wavefront crossing. Combining measurements from $p$ strategically placed observation centers via an ensemble log-likelihood sum, a single broken bond is identified with an 82-fold margin over the next candidate on a $7\times7$ lattice. Extending to realistic coupling degradation ($δJ = -0.20$) and up to 8 simultaneous faults, the integrated log-ratio $Λ(v) = \ln(\mathcal{B}(v)/\mathcal{N}(v))$ achieves a per-bond detection rate above 90\% in a single seismic pass using only 6 simulations. An iterative re-scan strategy progressively resolves multi-bond cases as the signal clears with each recalibration pass. The method requires no model assumptions and no knowledge of the perturbation type or magnitude; the detection is deliberately blind.

papers.title: End-line Fourier restriction for hyperbolic surfaces in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove new bilinear adjoint Fourier restriction estimates for pairs of separated rectangles associated to a hyperbolic surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then employ these bilinear estimates to prove Fourier extension inequalities along the (sharp) parabolic scaling line for any smooth hyperbolic 2-surface that is either the graph of a polynomial or that obeys a mild finite type condition.

papers.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
papers.abstract: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the $μ$- and $y$-distortions expected from $Λ$CDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: Riemannian geodesic motions and null foliations
papers.abstract: We study the non-collision problem: given a unit vector field $V$ on a complete Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, under what conditions on $V$ are the maps $F_t(p)=\exp_p(tV(p))$ injective for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$? If such a vector field exists, we call it a geodesic motion on $M$. This occurs, for instance, when $V$ defines a geodesic foliation of $M$, in which case, the geodesic motion is called stationary. We show that geodesic motions on the Euclidean plane are necessarily stationary, that generic geodesic motions on round spheres are non-stationary, and that compact hyperbolic $3$-manifolds admit no geodesic motions. The non-collision problem has a Lorentzian interpretation: geodesic motions on $M$ correspond to one-dimensional null geodesic foliations of the spacetime $(M\times\mathbb{R},g-dt^2)$. In the second part of the paper, we focus on codimension-one lightlike geodesic foliations of anti-de Sitter space $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,n}$. We give a complete characterization of such foliations by means of causal curves in the Einstein universe and prove rigidity in the projective anti-de Sitter case. The last part of the paper is dedicated to the study of one-dimensional geodesic foliations of $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,2}$. We give a complete characterization when the foliation contains at least one timelike leaf.

papers.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

papers.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
papers.abstract: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic. In addition, we prove that a dynamically convex Reeb pseudo-rotation on a sphere has at least two non-degenerate, irrationally elliptic orbits.

papers.title: Gusto: a toolkit for compatible finite element dynamical cores
papers.abstract: Gusto is a tool for rapid prototyping of new algorithms based on compatible finite element methods for discretising the fluid equations in the dynamical core of weather and climate models. In this context, the development of new algorithms typically follows a path that involves testing on a hierarchy of simpler equation sets sharing important features of the mathematical structure of the equation set solved by the dynamical core. Gusto provides compatible finite element spatial discretisations of the hierarchy of equation sets, along with a range of timestepping schemes. The code is modular so that different spatial and temporal discretisations can be combined and the same schemes can be applied to any of the equation sets. This facilitates fair comparison of the schemes and makes the extension of any algorithmic developments to the more complex equation sets more straightforward. In this paper we present Gusto to the community by describing the algorithms implemented in Gusto and showcasing their performance through a variety of test problems commonly used in numerical weather prediction.

papers.title: Recursive Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz
papers.abstract: The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We extend this recursion to constrained problems by building on the quantum alternating operator ansatz, which restricts the evolution to feasible solutions through a feasible initial state and feasibility-preserving mixers. However, every elimination alters the feasibility structure, so that such a mixer for the original problem generally fails to be one for the subproblems. Previous extensions to Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover sidestep this with tailored reduction rules that keep every subproblem within the original problem class. We resolve this by identifying, for a given constraint structure, a broader problem class that is closed under all eliminations, and by efficiently constructing feasible initial states and feasibility-preserving mixers for every class member. We do so for monotone constraints, such as for the knapsack problem, for linear equality constraints with polynomially bounded weights, including Hamming weight constraints, and for combinations of equality constraints with a single inequality constraint, such as the cardinality-constrained knapsack problem. Conversely, we show that these restrictions cannot be lifted in general without leaving the realm of efficient constructions. Exact simulations on knapsack and vertex-weighted max-bisection instances demonstrate that our recursive scheme can outperform both its non-recursive counterpart and penalty-based QAOA and RQAOA.

papers.title: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
papers.abstract: We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $Δ_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $Σ_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology. Motivic conjectures relating algebraic cycles to special values of $L$-functions suggest that $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonzero in Chow. More precisely, we prove that the Chow nonvanishing of $\mathsf{Q}$ follows from a conjecture of Harder concerning the failure of the Manin--Drinfeld principle in genus 2. We prove that $\mathsf{Q}$ vanishes in cohomology by pairing with generators of the tautological ring. To prove $\mathsf{Q}$ is not in the set of $3$-spin relations requires an argument involving the $Σ_{14}$-representation-theoretic properties of the $3$-spin relations and the cohomology of local systems on $\mathcal{A}_2$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$. Parallel constructions for other moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ are discussed in the paper. There are many open questions.

papers.title: Extrinsic Representation of the Partial Ricci Flow
papers.abstract: The partial Ricci flow (PRF) modifies the Riemannian metric on a foliation on a distribution orthogonal to the leaves. In this work we develop extrinsic representations of PRF on geodesic foliations (twisted/warped products, weak K-contact and weak \b{eta}-Kenmotsu manifolds) and analyze model cases where PRF admits closed-form solutions. Using the convergence of PRF on model cases, we construct its extrinsic representations initialized by rotational hypersurfaces in Euclidean space as well as parallel curved surfaces and ellipsoids. The extrinsic viewpoint for PRF provides new tools for studying curvature-driven dynamics on foliations, with potential applications to calculus of moving surfaces and mathematical physics.

papers.title: Sampling recovery for intersections of Lipschitz classes in the low-smoothness regime
papers.abstract: We study sampling recovery in $L_p(\mathbb T^d)$ for intersections of Lipschitz classes defined by smoothness conditions in two different metrics $L_p$ and $L_q$, where $1\le p<q\le\infty$. Our focus is on the low-smoothness range, where the $L_p$-smoothness does not exceed the classical continuity threshold $d/p$. We determine the exact orders of the sampling numbers for both linear and general recovery algorithms, including critical smoothness cases in which logarithmic factors appear or uniform convergence fails. To analyze sampling approximation in the low-smoothness range, we establish new inequalities for averaged moduli of smoothness with different integrability parameters and derive sharp estimates for these moduli and the corresponding semi-discrete measures of smoothness. These estimates provide error bounds for linear sampling operators acting on functions whose smoothness may lie below the classical continuity threshold. Finally, we determine the Kolmogorov widths of the intersection classes and quantify the gap between optimal sampling recovery and approximation by finite-dimensional subspaces.

papers.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

papers.title: Finite-time spectral enhancement of transient quantum thermometry
papers.abstract: Transient quantum thermometry extracts temperature information before a probe reaches thermal equilibrium. We study how finite interaction times affect thermometric precision for a harmonic-oscillator probe prepared in a number state and weakly coupled to a thermal bosonic reservoir. A second-order time-convolutionless master equation retains the finite-time reservoir response, allowing modes away from the probe frequency to shape the populations and their temperature dependence. For the baseline parameters, this response raises the quantum Fisher information about fivefold above the Markovian prediction, in agreement with an exact solution of the model. When the probability of leaving the initial state is small, we derive an analytical condition for this enhancement. To assess its operational significance, we examine the temperature information acquired per unit time. Under the exact dynamics, this rate is largest within the reservoir memory time. With negligible preparation and readout overhead, the optimum is about five times the best Markovian rate and 30 times an upper bound on the equilibrium rate. The advantage survives smooth switching, although overhead and longer coupling ramps reduce it.

papers.title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
papers.abstract: The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of Möbius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$. Our destination formula computes it as the closure of a unipotent orbit, determined by the Cartan data and a bounded Levi factor. The stratified convergence principle organises these destinations into families of translated Schubert varieties attached to boundary points of a compactification of the group. Over the complex numbers, the destination relation is the support of Brion's limiting graphs in the wonderful compactification, providing scheme structures, multidegrees and diagonal intersections. For discrete groups, the union of destination relations determines proper discontinuity and whether a largest domain exists. It relates Quint's flag limit set, Conze--Guivarc'h, Kulkarni and Myrberg sets to the recurrent set, while balanced choices of cells yield domains for every discrete subgroup, without Anosov hypotheses. For symmetric-power actions of non-elementary Kleinian groups on $\mathbb{CP}^N$, we compute the largest domain by a multiplicity bound at points of the classical limit set; for $N\ge3$ it strictly contains the Kulkarni domain, which equals the equicontinuity region. We also obtain nonempty largest domains for Zariski-dense cusped Hitchin groups with unipotent elements, and examples of strongly irreducible groups with no largest domain.

papers.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
papers.abstract: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

papers.title: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
papers.abstract: Let $q=2^m$ for an even $m\geq 6$ and let $d=s(q-1)+1$ with $4s\equiv5\pmod{q+1}$. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period $q^2-1$ and its $d$-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values $q(i-1)-1$ for $0\leq i\leq 6$, and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of $K_m(1)$ and $K_m(ω)$, where $K_m(\cdot)$ is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $ω$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_4$.

papers.title: Learning monotone game-theoretic linear MPC
papers.abstract: We propose a method to learn a game-theoretic model predictive control (GT-MPC) law by imitation from input and output data of a running multi-agent system. By interpreting the recorded inputs as the first moves of the equilibria of a game played by the agents, we learn the GT-MPC weights under hard input constraints and soft output constraints, without requiring the agents to reveal their objectives. We also impose that the resulting generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problem is strongly monotone, which ensures the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium and, hence, that the learned GT-MPC law is well defined and can be evaluated efficiently online by variational GNE-seeking algorithms for linear-quadratic games. Moreover, strong monotonicity implies that the equilibrium is almost everywhere differentiable with respect to the references and the weights, which enables automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization. In addition, we promote closed-loop stability of the unconstrained equilibrium feedback by incorporating a penalty that involves a jointly learned quadratic Lyapunov function. Learning a GT-MPC formulation enables us to explain the agents' objectives, reproduce their behavior in simulation in new scenarios, optimize their set-points, design mechanisms, and enforce additional constraints. A numerical example illustrates the approach.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity (MF) formulation of Operator Inference (OpInf) for learning non-intrusive, physics-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of nonlinear dynamical systems. OpInf learns reduced operators from projections of snapshot data by solving a least squares regression problem. However, generating high-fidelity snapshots can be computationally expensive, limiting parameter coverage and the temporal extent of training trajectories for many aerospace applications, which can lead to inaccurate or unstable ROM predictions. This work proposes MF-OpInf, which combines limited high-fidelity snapshots with more plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variates-inspired MF least squares formulation to learn a single set of reduced operators across multiple trajectories. Low-fidelity trajectories provide additional parameter coverage and extend beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. The low-fidelity snapshots are also used to construct an improved reduced basis through weighted proper orthogonal decomposition. We demonstrate MF-OpInf on a nonlinear reaction-diffusion problem with parametrized sinusoidal forcing and a two-dimensional incompressible flow past a cylinder with a parametrized inlet pulse. In these experiments, under an equal training simulation budget, MF-OpInf reduces the mean relative prediction error at unseen parameters by up to $87\%$ for the reaction-diffusion problem and $28\%$ for the cylinder flow problem over the test time regime, which extends beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. These results demonstrate that MF-OpInf can improve temporal extrapolation and prediction at unseen parameters without increasing the training simulation budget.

papers.title: Wasserstein geometry of analytic cycle spaces
papers.abstract: We use optimal transport to define an intrinsic distance on connected components of the Barlet space of analytic cycles on a compact Kähler manifold, by associating to each cycle its normalized volume measure. We prove that any two cycles in the same connected component can be joined by a deformation of finite Wasserstein length, and that the resulting metric is complete and geodesic. On the locus of smooth reduced cycles at regular parameter points, Wasserstein lengths and energies coincide with those of the normalized Weil--Petersson metric. The construction thus gives a transport interpretation of Weil--Petersson geometry and extends beyond it to components containing no smooth reduced cycles.

papers.title: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
papers.abstract: Let $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$ enumerates the number of $k$-colored simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions. In this article, we establish some new infinite families of congruences modulo prime $p$, $p\geq5$ and modulo powers of 5 for $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$. For instance, for each $n\geq0$, $0\leqα\leq{2k-2}$ and $k\geq1$, \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_{(5^{2k-1},5^{2k-1})}^2\big(5^{2k+α-1}n+\frac{9\cdot5^{2k+α-1}-2\cdot5^{2k-1}+1}{12}\big)q^n\equiv& 0\pmod{5^{k+\left[\fracα{2}\right]}} \end{align*}

papers.title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellensätze with Operator Coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.

papers.title: A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $ε$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.

papers.title: Isolation of $k$-cliques in uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: A copy of a hypergraph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any integers $k$ and $r$ with $2 \leq r \leq k$, let $K_k^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is $[k] = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (that is, the edges of $K_k^r$ are the $r$-element subsets of $[k]$). Given an $r$-uniform $m$-edge hypergraph $H$, the $K_k^r$-isolation number of $H$, denoted by $ι(H, K_k^r)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $H$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $K_k^r$-copies contained by $H$ (equivalently, $H-N[D]$ contains no $K_k^r$-copy). We prove that if $H$ is connected and not a $K_k^r$-copy, then $$ι(H, K^r_k) \le \left \lfloor \frac{(r-1)m + 1}{(r-1)(\binom{k}{r}+1) + 1} \right \rfloor.$$ The bound is best possible. This is a solution to a problem of Li, Zhang and Ye. We also provide an alternative proof for $r < k$. Both proofs introduce new ideas for establishing bounds on isolation parameters.

papers.title: Convergence Properties of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, and Gain Dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.

papers.title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
papers.abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology.
